abstract: SHFL (Shiftless) is an interferon-stimulated antiviral factor implicated in multiple modes of viral restriction, including inhibition of -1 programmed ribosomal frameshifting (-1 PRF). However, how SHFL interfaces with host post-transcriptional regulatory pathways remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that SHFL promotes mRNA turnover through the CCR4-NOT-associated 5'-3' mRNA decay pathway. SHFL reduced the abundance of -1 PRF-containing reporters and induced mRNA decay when tethered to the 3' untranslated region, indicating that SHFL-mediated RNA turnover can be triggered independently of the -1 PRF context. Mechanistically, SHFL interacted with endogenous CNOT3 and directly associated with the reconstituted CNOT1/2/3 NOT module in vitro. Functional analyses further showed that CNOT3 is required for efficient SHFL-mediated mRNA decay. In contrast, SHFL-mediated repression of -1 PRF-dependent translation remained intact in CNOT3 knockout cells, supporting a mechanistic separation between SHFL-mediated mRNA decay and -1 PRF translational repression. Transcriptome analyses under non-infectious conditions further suggested that SHFL overexpression is associated with selective changes in inflammatory and interferon-responsive gene-expression modules. Together, these findings identify CNOT3-dependent engagement of the CCR4-NOT mRNA decay machinery as a post-transcriptional mechanism used by SHFL, while positioning -1 PRF repression as a separable SHFL activity.
